thread.title: Higher Prices Drive Apple to Record Quarterly Revenue -- Earnings Review

author: morningstar.com
title: Higher Prices Drive Apple to Record Quarterly Revenue -- Earnings Review
text:
By Tripp Mickle and Austen Hufford
Apple Inc. (AAPL) reported results for its fiscal first quarter after the market closed Thursday. Here's what you need to know:
EARNINGS: The company had net income of $20.07 billion, or $3.89 a share, compared with a $17.89 billion, or $3.36 a share, in the year-ago quarter. Analysts had expected earnings per share of $3.86.
REVENUE: Total revenue rose 13% to $88.29 billion in the quarter, above the $87.06 billion expected by analysts.
SHARES: In post-market trading, shares of Apple rose 1.9%. Shares have risen 0.5% in the past three months.
IPHONE: Apple's latest phone, the iPhone X, was released in November at a starting price of $1,000. It lifted Apple's average phone selling price and helped drive smartphone revenue to a record $61.58 billion for the three months through Dec. 30, up 13% from a year earlier. The number of iPhones it sold fell 1% to 77.3 million units.
CASH: Apple CFO Luca Maestri tells WSJ that the company has $285 billion in cash and $122 billion in debt. In mid-January the company announced it would pay $38 billion in taxes on the $252 billion it holds overseas, but it hasn't said how much of that money it will bring back to the U.S. or outlined what will be returned to shareholders through buybacks or dividends. Mr. Maestri said the company is targeting a "net cash neutral" position over time.
OUTLOOK: Apple said it expects revenue of between $60 billion and $62 billion for the current quarter. That would represent a rise from a year earlier, but is well below analysts' recent consensus estimate of $66.54 billion, a number that had fallen over the past several weeks as analysts lowered estimates on concerns about demand for the iPhone X and uncertainty around the new iPhone 8 and 8 Plus models launched in September.
